children: Benchmark indices opened sharply lower on Thursday morning, with the Sensex falling 631.58 points, or 0.84 per cent, to 74,196.67 against its previous close of 74,828.25, after opening at 74,272.40. The Nifty 50 dropped 214 points, or 0.91 per cent, to 23,232.80 as of 9.21 am, against its previous close of 23,446.80 and an open of 23,221.80, as a spike in Brent crude prices above $102 per barrel and a rise in US 10-year Treasury yields to 5.11 per cent weighed on investor sentiment.

Financial stocks bore the brunt of the sell-off. HDFC Life Insurance was the top loser on the Nifty 50, falling 6.28 per cent to ₹526.25 from a previous close of ₹561.50. Bajaj Finance slid 5.21 per cent to ₹988.80 from ₹1,043.20, while Axis Bank declined 4.13 per cent to ₹1,191.90 from ₹1,243.20. Bajaj Finserv dropped 3.54 per cent to ₹1,781.20 from ₹1,846.50, and SBI Life Insurance fell 2.18 per cent to ₹1,721.60 from ₹1,760.00, making the financial services and insurance space the primary drag on the indices.

"The sharp spike in Brent crude above $102 and the US 10-year bond yield rising to 5.11 per cent will weigh on the market today," said Dr V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments. “So long as these two global headwinds remain, the prospects of a smart recovery in the market appear remote."

Only three Nifty 50 constituents were trading in the green in early trade. Tech Mahindra gained 0.87 per cent to ₹1,570.50 from a previous close of ₹1,557.00, making it the top gainer. Sun Pharmaceutical Industries edged up 0.13 per cent to ₹1,867.50 from ₹1,865.00, while NTPC added a marginal 0.03 per cent to ₹326.10 from ₹326.00.

The broader global backdrop triggered the gap-down start. Wall Street closed lower overnight as strong US business-activity data revived expectations of a further Federal Reserve rate increase, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield above 5 per cent and weighing on technology stocks. Asian markets were showing mixed trends in early trade.

"Indian equities are likely to face a sharp gap-down opening, with Gift Nifty around 23,267, down 178 points," said Hitesh Tailor, Technical Research Analyst at Choice Broking. "Global sentiment has weakened as Wall Street ended lower amid rising US Treasury yields and an increasing Dollar Index, adding pressure on emerging-market sentiment."

Geopolitical uncertainty compounded the pressure. Conflicting signals from Iranian officials regarding the Strait of Hormuz kept crude oil prices sensitive, with WTI trading around $91–$92 per barrel and Brent above the $100 mark. Markets were also watching a scheduled meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, which could have implications for trade and technology policy.

On the institutional front, both foreign and domestic investors were net buyers in the previous session on September 23. Foreign Institutional Investors purchased equities worth ₹1,617 crore, while Domestic Institutional Investors bought ₹2,341 crore, providing some cushion against the global headwinds.

Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, a SEBI-registered wealth-tech firm, noted that "...a rebound in crude oil prices amid renewed uncertainty surrounding the US-Iran diplomatic process, coupled with a rise in US Treasury yields, is likely to prompt some profit-taking after the market's recent gains."

Technically, the Nifty is approaching a critical support zone. Pabitro Mukherjee, Deputy Vice President-Research at Bajaj Broking, said the index is likely to trade in a broad range of 23,115–23,650 in the coming sessions. "A breach below Tuesday's low of 23,285 will open downside towards last week's low of 23,116 levels," he cautioned.

On the banking index, the Bank Nifty closed at 56,548.90 in the previous session, gaining 333 points or 0.60 per cent, but was under pressure Wednesday morning. The index must hold the 56,000–56,200 band to prevent weakness from broadening, with resistance seen at 56,700–57,000. "A decisive break below 56,000 could revive selling pressure and expose the index to lower support levels," said Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, Founder and CEO of HST Wealth.

Separately, the NSE listing was drawing considerable market attention. "If the NSE stock becomes available in today's trade at a fair price, that would be a good opportunity for long-term investors to have a blue chip in their portfolio," said Vijayakumar of Geojit.

The India VIX stood at 10.37, indicating that the market remained lightly hedged despite rising external risks, while the Put-Call Ratio at 1.01 reflected balanced positioning with no strong directional bias as of the previous session's close.

title: Sensex, Nifty slide over 0.8% as rising crude, US bond yields rattle markets; financials lead losses
